name: Grid transfer
summary: A grid laid over a subject or a photograph and a matching grid on the canvas; the painter copies the picture square by square.
how: Draw a grid of 1 to 5 cm over the reference and a grid of the same ratio on the canvas.
Copy the contour of each square, one at a time, so that the whole picture stays in the right place.
Paint each square at the same focus, with an even grain over the full surface.
Scale up by a fixed ratio, for example 10:1.

origin.note: Leon Battista Alberti describes a veil of threads that gives a grid over the scene in De pictura.

adoptions.via: Albrecht Dürer prints draughtsmen who draw through a frame with a grid in Underweysung der Messung.
Chuck Close works from a gridded photograph in Big Self-Portrait.
